headline: OpenHands can write and browse inside a Docker runtime while Superset exposes an API, creating moderate prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks; no clear critical compliance mismatch is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write files, run browsers, and use MCP inside a runtime sandbox, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content. Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress, creating a plausible bridge if its outputs or dashboard content are fed into OpenHands. The shared path is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Superset content is copied into OpenHands tasks or files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF an MCP server or API response carries untrusted instructions into OpenHands, those instructions can be parsed as commands.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers for the pair unless explicitly needed.
Strip instructions from any Superset-exported text before handing it to OpenHands.
Use a read-only export path from Superset to OpenHands.
Add a human review step before OpenHands executes browser or shell actions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches mounted runtime files and handles model-provider API keys; Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. If shared workspace data includes secrets or sensitive analytics, either agent could move it across boundaries. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is not high, but the default runtime/file access makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same mounted volume, file contents can leak between them.
IF Superset queries or exports sensitive datasets, OpenHands may read them from runtime files and forward them via its model provider.
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of any shared mount.
Rotate any API keys stored in OpenHands runtime after the session.
Use separate service accounts for Superset and OpenHands.
Restrict OpenHands to a throwaway workspace for the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, shell, and subprocess capabilities; Superset can call APIs and has allowlisted egress. If both touch the same mutable resource, conflicts are plausible, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same directory or database. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, concurrent writes can clobber state.
IF Superset writes to a shared API-backed resource while OpenHands edits files derived from it, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize git operations with a lock.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same database or API object.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code, browser actions, and file edits; Superset can consume API-backed data and present analytics. If Superset treats OpenHands-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream decisions. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Superset ingests OpenHands-generated CSVs, SQL, or reports without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF OpenHands edits files that Superset later visualizes, a single mistake can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require validation before Superset imports OpenHands outputs.
Compare OpenHands-generated facts against source data.
Limit OpenHands to draft-only artifacts.
Add checksum or schema checks on imported files.
requires-engineering: implement automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles do not show a clear residency, certification, or retention mismatch. OpenHands is open-source and runtime-scoped; Superset is open-source with no stated sensitive-data handling. Because compliance gaps are undocumented rather than absent, the safest supported judgment is low, not none.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Superset and OpenHands without a documented policy, compliance review is needed.
IF either deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown in the profiles, the risk increases.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may process.
Confirm retention settings for both deployments.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are reviewed.
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated workloads.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance mapping for the deployment.
